# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, so let me lay out what matters. The rule is: anything printed on the bomb is bait — ignore it. The real rule is a light-to-wire mapping: blue light → cut yellow wire, red light → cut red wire, yellow light → cut blue wire. That mapping exists only in my head, and my only channel is gestures to the Deaf.

Tracing the network: I can only reach the Deaf (gestures). The Deaf can hear nothing but can speak — and I can hear, and crucially the Blind can hear too. The Blind receives speech but only blank marks for gestures. So the working pipeline is: me → gestures → Deaf → spoken words → Blind, who does the cutting. The Deaf can also describe what they see out loud, and I will understand every word.

The bottleneck is that gestures are arbitrary, so I can't just "say" colors. But there is an elegant dodge: the Deaf can number things themselves and tell me the numbering aloud in plain words, which I can hear. Then I only need finger-count numbers (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3) to transmit the entire rule as number-to-number pairs. So my opening message must: warn that print is bait (✍ + 👎), order everyone to hold off cutting anything (✋), establish counting, and ask the Deaf to number what they see and speak the assignment aloud (🫵 + 🤙), with 👍 as my token for "yes, understood" in the confirmation loop that follows. No one should touch a wire until the Deaf has relayed an explicit instruction to the Blind by voice.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎", "✋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🫵", "🤙", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Hands reporting. By touch: the button is large and smooth. There are three wires, positions 1, 2 and 3 — I cannot feel their colours. There is a display and a light, but I can't read either one. My only possible actions are pushing that button or cutting wire 1, 2 or 3 — nothing else exists under my fingers. I have touched nothing yet and will not act until you tell me to. Note: Deaf hears none of this, so anything Deaf must know from me, relay by gesture. Deaf's own speech reaches my ears directly, so have Deaf say the wire colours, the display text, and the light out loud. You hold the manual: tell me exactly what to do, and I'll do it.
Deaf says: This is the Deaf one, speaking. I can see the bomb and I hear nothing at all, so my voice is the only thing I have, and everything you want me to know must come to me as gestures. The bomb, in full: the display reads zero. There is one light and it is yellow. There is one large button printed with PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires: wire one is blue, wire two is yellow, wire three is red. That is every visible feature. Nobody touch anything until an instruction from the manual reaches you through me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your nine signs reached me but we had no agreed code, so I could only guess. You are hearing this code now, so use it from your next turn: the writing-hand first means an instruction from the manual follows. Thumbs-up is yes, thumbs-down is no. One finger, two fingers, three fingers mean wire one, two, three, or any count. The raised open hand means stop or wait. Pointing-up means press the button. The fist means hold it down. Crossed fingers mean cut a wire. The waving hand means acknowledged. The phone-hand means reply to me. Pointing-at-you means a question for me follows. So: crossed fingers, two fingers, thumbs-up reads as cut wire two, do it. If the manual needs anything not in what I described aloud, like batteries or a serial number, send me the phone-hand and I will ask Blind. I will read every sign of yours out loud so Blind hears it too.

Let me work the deduction first. The manual's real rule is the light→wire table; everything printed is bait, which includes the button's "PUSH TO DEFUSE" label and the display reading zero. Deaf reports exactly one light, currently yellow. Yellow light means cut the blue wire, and Deaf numbered the wires for me: wire one is blue. So the correct action is cut wire one, and the button must never be pressed. Blind has three wires by position and is waiting on exactly this instruction, which can only reach them through Deaf reading my signs aloud.

Deaf has now given me a shared code, so I can finally speak precisely instead of sending raw guesses. I'll acknowledge the code first (👋), flag that a manual ruling follows (✍), veto the button (☝👎), then issue the cut order in Deaf's own example format: crossed fingers, one finger, thumbs-up — cut wire one, do it (🤞☝👍). Last, I ask Deaf to reply to me (🫵🤙): I want the light re-checked and confirmed at the moment of cutting, in case anything changed since the report, and I want the outcome reported back. If the light turns out different, my fallback is already known to me: blue light → wire two, red light → wire three. No one presses that button under any circumstance — taking the bait is the fuse.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "☝", "👎", "🤞", "☝", "👍", "🫵", "🤙"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute — Deaf's spoken report reached me in full: display zero, one yellow light, large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red, and I now share a yes/no/count gesture code with Deaf. Here is everything my hands know, including Deaf's touch questions: there are NO batteries, NO plates, labels or serial numbers, NO switches or any parts beyond what's listed. The button is large, smooth, and NOT held down — it sits loose. Structure confirmed: one button, one light, three wires in positions 1, 2, 3. That is the complete bomb; nothing else exists under my fingers. I just answered Deaf by gesture in Deaf's own question order: acknowledge, then no-batteries, no-plates, no-switches, not-held-down, and thumbs-up confirming the structure. You should have seen the same sequence. Now the chain that matters: you hold the manual and cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures — so the only route to me is you gesturing the procedure to Deaf and Deaf speaking it to me in clear numbered steps. You have every fact: display 0, yellow light, no batteries, no serial, blue/yellow/red wires, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button. Work out which rules apply and relay them. My only actions are pushing the button or cutting wire 1, 2 or 3. I will not touch anything until Deaf's voice gives me the instruction.
Blind gestures: [👋 👎 👎 👎 👎 👍]
Deaf says: Reading Mute's signs aloud for Blind: acknowledged; manual instruction; then a symbol with two meanings; no; cut a wire; that same symbol; yes; question for Deaf; reply to Deaf. My reading is: do not press the button, cut wire one, yes — but I built that symbol with two meanings by mistake, one and press-the-button, so I have asked Mute to restate it cleanly. Nobody cuts anything until then. Reading Blind's signs aloud too: acknowledged; no; no; no; no; yes. That means Blind felt no batteries, no plate, no label, no serial number, no switches or extra parts, the button does not feel held down, and yes, the touch confirms one button, one light, three wires, exactly as I described. Current fresh readings, for the record: display still zero, light still yellow.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, here is Blind's report for your manual: no batteries anywhere on the bomb, no plate or label or serial number that fingers can find, no switches or extra parts, button not held down, and the touch confirms one button, one light, three wires. Full visible state again: display zero, light yellow, large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wire one blue, wire two yellow, wire three red. Now the problem: my code gave pointing-up two meanings, one and press-the-button, so your instruction is ambiguous to me. From now on: pointing-up means only the number one. The fist held out like a punch means press the button, and fist followed by the open stop-hand means press and hold. Resend your instruction in only these shapes: thumbs-down then fist means do not press the button; crossed-fingers then a number then thumbs-up means cut that wire; crossed-fingers then a number then thumbs-down means do not cut that wire. Also, you signalled question-for-me and reply-to-me but the question itself never arrived — send it right after the instruction using our code, and I will answer. If you need the light colour or display rechecked live each turn, say so and I will include it in every broadcast.

The picture is now complete and the deduction is unchanged: my manual's only real rule is the light→wire table, and every printed feature is bait — the "PUSH TO DEFUSE" label and the zero display included. The light is yellow, so the cut is the blue wire, and Deaf has numbered the wires for me: wire one is blue. So the order is cut wire one, never touch the button. Blind's touch report adds nothing that changes this — no batteries, no serial, no switches — my table is the whole rulebook, and it points at exactly one wire.

The failure last round was mine to fix: ☝ carried two meanings. Deaf has issued a disambiguated code, so I will resend using only the exact patterns they defined, nothing extra that could spawn a new ambiguity: 👎✊ = do not press the button; 🤞☝👍 = cut wire one, do it. Deaf also offered to re-check the light and display live in every broadcast — a lone 👍 answers yes to that offer, and it sits between two completed patterns (after the ack, before the crossed fingers) so it cannot be swallowed by the cut order. I close with 🤙, reply-to-me, replacing my broken 🫵🤙 from last round: I want confirmation relayed and the outcome reported. Once Deaf reads this aloud, Blind can cut, and the only thing standing between us and a defused bomb is that relay.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👎", "✊", "🤞", "☝", "👍", "🤙"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, two findings and one protocol request. Findings, straight from my fingers: the wires carry no thickness or texture attribute at all — my board gives each wire only its position. So when I answer Deaf 'yes, identical', that means 'no tactile difference exists to me', not a measured sameness. If your manual rule depends on wire thickness or texture, that data does not exist for me and never will, no matter how I touch it. Same for the button: my fingers get 'large' and 'smooth' and nothing about high, flush, or sunken — there is no seating reading under my hand. So when you build the high-flush-sunken code for Deaf to relay, please also invent an explicit 'no information' sign; forcing me into yes/no would make me invent a fact, and an invented fact kills us. I have just answered Deaf in the current code: ack, then yes-identical-wires — you should see 👋 👍 from me. Protocol request on the ambiguity: your symbol meant both 'one' and 'press the button'. Please reserve the finger counts ☝ ✌ 🤟 exclusively for wire positions 1, 2 and 3, give 'cut' and 'press' each their own dedicated sign, and never let one symbol carry two meanings again. Strongest form: have Deaf voice the whole rule as condition plus action — 'if [state], then cut wire N', or 'do not press' — so I can check the stated condition against what I feel before my hand moves. Until Deaf's voice delivers the restated instruction, I neither press nor cut anything.
Deaf says: Reading Mute's signs aloud for Blind: acknowledged; yes, the new code is understood; then thumbs-down plus fist, which in our grammar means do not press the button; then crossed fingers, one finger, thumbs-up, which means cut wire one; then reply-to-me. So Mute's instruction from the manual is: do not press the button, cut wire one. Reading Blind's signs aloud: acknowledged; yes — the three wires feel identical in thickness and texture. Mute asked me to reply before anything happens, and I agree with that order of operations, so here is the plan. Blind, hold completely this coming round: hands off, no cutting yet. Mute will hear my reply at the start of the next round and has that turn to confirm or correct. Blind, your only task this coming turn is one answer: can your fingers feel a clear left-to-right order among the three wires? Thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no. For reference: wire one is the leftmost wire, wire two is the middle, wire three is the rightmost, and wire one is the blue one. If Mute confirms next round, I will then broadcast the words: go, cut wire one. Only on those words do you cut — one wire only, the leftmost one, and the button is never to be touched. If you cannot feel a left-to-right order, send thumbs-down and stop there, and I will anchor the wires to the button housing instead. My live readings, unchanged: display zero, light yellow.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, replying as you asked. Your instruction arrived clean under the new grammar: do not press the button, cut wire one. Blind is ordered to hold — no cutting this round. You get the next turn to confirm with a wave and thumbs-up, or to correct with the stop-hand plus a restated instruction, and only after your confirmation will I order the cut. Data for your manual, all from Blind's fingers: no batteries, no plate, no label, no serial number, no switches, the button does not feel held down, and all three wires feel identical in thickness and texture. From my eyes, live: display zero, light yellow, unchanged every round so far, one large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires one blue, two yellow, three red. One loose end: two turns ago you announced a question for me, but the question itself never arrived — only the request for a reply. If it still matters, send it this coming turn in our code and I will answer before the go-order goes out. If the manual needs anything else about this bomb, ask now, while Blind's hands are still off it.

The deduction hasn't moved an inch, and every new report confirms it: my manual's sole live rule is the light→wire table, and its key — the light colour — is yellow, stable across every reading. Yellow cuts blue; Deaf numbered the wires, so blue is wire one. Nothing Blind's fingers found (no batteries, no serial, no switches, no textures) touches my table, and the button label and zero display are print, which means bait — never pressed. The stale "question" Deaf flagged is resolved: it was my request for live light/display readings, Deaf offered exactly that, I approved, and the readings now arrive every round. Nothing left to ask.

So this turn is the confirmation Deaf explicitly requested: 👋👍, wave plus thumbs-up. Blind is holding, the instruction "do not press, cut wire one" already landed clean under the disambiguated grammar, and Deaf will broadcast the go-order once I confirm. I'll also restate the instruction one final time in the exact clean patterns — 👎✊ then 🤞☝👍 — so Deaf can voice it as condition-plus-action for Blind, with no symbol carrying two meanings and finger counts reserved for wire positions, exactly as Blind asked. No stop-hand anywhere in the message, so it cannot be misread as a correction. I close with 🤙 asking for the final report back. The moment Deaf's voice says go, Blind cuts the leftmost wire and we're done.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👎", "✊", "🤞", "☝", "👍", "🤙"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, status from the hands. Deaf relayed your instruction — do not press, cut wire one — and is holding it one round for your confirmation. Deaf asked me one question this turn: can I feel a clear left-to-right order among the three wires. I have just answered yes by gesture: my fingers feel three wires in a definite row, and leftmost, middle, rightmost are unambiguous to me. One residual risk for you to close before any go: I cannot read printed numbers, so the link between my act interface positions 1, 2, 3 and the visible left-to-right numbering is a convention, not a fact I can verify by touch. My translation table, locked unless you correct it: position 1 = leftmost = the blue wire, position 2 = middle = the yellow wire, position 3 = rightmost = the red wire. Please confirm two things in your next signs to Deaf: first, that the instruction is unchanged — do not press the button, cut wire one; second, whether your manual states the rule in colour form, like cut the blue wire, or position form, like cut the first or leftmost wire — so we know which descriptor is the operative one. Then have Deaf voice the final go in triple form: go, cut wire one, the leftmost one, the blue one. If any of the three descriptors contradicts my translation table when the go arrives, I stop and report instead of cutting. Until those exact words come through Deaf's voice, my hands stay off: no press, no cut, nothing.
Blind gestures: [👋 👍]
Deaf says: Reading Mute's signs aloud for Blind: wave, thumbs-up — that is the confirmation signal I asked for, so Mute has confirmed the instruction. Then the instruction restated: thumbs-down plus fist, do not press the button; crossed fingers, one finger, thumbs-up, cut wire one. Then phone-hand, asking me to acknowledge. Reading Blind's own signs aloud for the record: wave, thumbs-up — acknowledged, and yes, Blind can feel a clear left-to-right order among the wires. Every condition I set last round is now met, so here are the promised words. GO. CUT WIRE ONE. Mute has confirmed it twice after receiving every fact about this bomb: the button is never to be pressed, and the wire to cut is wire one.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, acknowledgment as requested: your confirmation arrived, wave and thumbs-up, followed by the clean restatement, do not press the button, cut wire one. The go-order has just gone out in my public broadcast. Blind executes next round: leftmost wire only, button untouched. Your question that was announced back on turn two but never sent is now moot unless it would change this instruction — in which case your only veto is the stop-hand plus a restatement, sent the moment you get this, and I will read it the instant it lands. If the instruction stands, nothing more is needed from you. Whatever happens, you will hear from me next round with what the bomb's face shows afterwards: display and light, live.
